Key Criticisms of the Strategy
• Lack of Actionable Details: The plan sets out no indicative budgets, establishes no formal delivery vehicle, defines no hard timetables, and states what should be done without specifying who will do it or with what resources.
• Narrow Public Sector Focus: While the strategy targets public bodies—covering roughly a quarter of the local workforce—it largely ignores economy-wide issues like small-and-medium enterprise (SME) adoption, workforce exposure, and regional productivity gaps.
• The Legislative and Border Dilemma: As noted by GovInsider, Northern Ireland sits in a regulatory gap between UK national legislation and the EU's strict approach (via the Republic of Ireland border), yet the strategy largely glosses over how businesses should navigate these conflicting rulebooks.
• Political and Public Pushback: Local bodies like Belfast City Council have refused to endorse the Stormont plan due to missing clarity on energy impacts, data centers, and a consultation tone criticized as unconvincing.

tweets.text:
The absolute difference in kind between the human intellect and the mere simulations that AI technology yields is a longstanding theme both of Christian philosophical anthropology (recently reiterated in Pope Leo XIV’s Magnifica Humanitas) and of secular philosophical critiques developed by thinkers like John Searle, Hubert Dreyfus, Roger Penrose, and many others. If there is any problem with the phrase “artificial intelligence,” it is with the word “intelligence,” not “artificial.” Indeed, calling it “artificial” at least has the merit of suggesting that it is a mere simulation, just as artificial grass is merely a simulation of grass. By contrast, “super intelligence” and the other phrases Trump uses here imply that AI technology does in fact have intelligence in the sense we do, and to a greater degree.

If Trump insists that this is so despite having no competence whatsoever to speak on the subject, that would be laughable but harmless enough if it were merely the expression of a personal opinion. But it is an outrage for him to try to use the power of his office to pressure those engaged in public discussion of this issue to adopt his favored terminology. Normalizing this usage can only facilitate the spread of the grave error of conflating AI with genuine intelligence. No self-respecting academic or public intellectual who agrees with the critiques of AI mentioned above should go along with this ridiculous novel usage. More importantly, no one who has any respect for the truth should do so.

tweets.text:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming our world in remarkable ways.

From healthcare to finance, its applications are vast and varied.

AI can analyze massive amounts of data much faster than any human could.

This capability allows for more accurate diagnoses and personalized treatment plans in medicine.

In finance, AI algorithms can detect fraudulent transactions in real-time.

This not only protects consumers but also enhances the security of financial systems.

Moreover, in the field of education, AI can tailor learning experiences to meet individual student needs.

Imagine a classroom where each student gets a personalized curriculum based on their strengths and weaknesses.

This could revolutionize how we approach education.

In the creative industries, AI is also making waves.

It helps in generating music, art, and even writing content.

While some fear that AI might replace human jobs, it is more likely to augment our capabilities.

By automating repetitive tasks, AI allows us to focus on more complex and creative endeavors.

However, ethical considerations surrounding AI cannot be overlooked.

Ensuring that AI is used responsibly and without bias is crucial.

As we continue to develop this technology, collaboration between technologists, ethicists, and policymakers is essential.

Building AI solutions requires a blend of data science, programming, and domain expertise.

For those interested in diving into AI, starting with online courses can be a great first step.

Platforms like Coursera and edX offer numerous resources to learn the basics.

Engaging in hands-on projects can also boost your skills and understanding.

As AI continues to evolve, staying informed about the latest trends and developments is vital.

The future of AI holds incredible potential, and we are just beginning to scratch the surface.

The Summit is over. Now the work begins!

Tony Perkins - FRC

Tue, Sep 29

Family Research Council - Header
Three days, one message: Pray, vote, stand.

Dear Wilda,

As our Pray Vote Stand Summit drew to a close on Saturday afternoon, I was filled with gratitude for all that God did this weekend.

More than a thousand people gathered at Cornerstone Chapel in Leesburg, Virginia, some flying from as far as Alaska and Canada, to pray, worship, and consider how Christians should respond biblically to some of the most pressing issues of our day.

We examined threats to our constitutional republic, including the growing influence of socialism and Sharia Law. We discussed what is unfolding in the Middle East, heard powerful testimonies from those affected by the on-going Biden-era chemical abortion drug policy, and considered how rapidly developing technologies like artificial intelligence raise fundamental questions about what it means to be human.

But our purpose was not simply to become better informed. We left with greater understanding to pray more specifically, act more wisely, and stand more faithfully.

And now we must take that mission beyond the Summit and into communities across America.

As we approach the midterm elections, decisions will be made that could shape our nation for years to come. Yoe Suárez, a Cuban exile and FRC's International Affairs Correspondent for The Washington Stand, brought a perspective few Americans have experienced firsthand:

"As someone who lived under socialism and under socialized medicine, I can tell you: a worse world is possible, and under socialism, is inevitable."

This is why Family Research Council works year-round to educate and equip Americans and lawmakers to understand the issues confronting our nation and to stand for biblical truth, in Washington and across America.

Wilda, your gift today will help FRC take the mission of Pray Vote Stand forward.

YES, TONY -- I STAND WITH FRC
https://t.co/GHAIadcCQ5
One story from this weekend illustrates why this work must reach beyond Washington.

We had the privilege of hearing from Andrew Coates and his parents, an everyday family from Fremont, Nebraska. Andrew is a 22-year-old trained EMT, who has served for two years as a volunteer firefighter. When he applied for a full-time firefighter position, however, his application was rejected, because he was homeschooled.

The original posting required only a high school diploma. But after Andrew applied, the qualification was changed to require graduation from an "accredited" school, meaning homeschoolers need not apply.

Homeschool graduates serve successfully in virtually every sector of American life and are accepted by colleges and universities across the country. Yet Andrew was denied even the opportunity to compete for a job for which he was otherwise qualified.

Since the story became public, support has poured in, and the family is hopeful that the city code will change its policy to recognize homeschooling as a legitimate high school education.

The city council takes up the issue tonight. Please join me in praying that God would move on the hearts of this council to yield to what is just and right.

But Andrew's story also illustrates something larger.

The challenges facing faith, family and freedom are not confined to Washington, D.C. They are showing up in school boards, city councils, workplaces and communities across America.

This is exactly why we are building Pray Vote Stand chapters -- church-anchored networks of believers biblically equipped to be "salt and light" (Matthew 5:13-14) in their local communities.

Our vision is ambitious:

A Pray Vote Stand chapter anchored in a church in every county in America.

Imagine thousands of communities where believers are praying together, understanding the issues, engaging their local leaders, and standing faithfully for biblical truth.

That is how the impact of a three-day Summit becomes a year-round movement.

And we cannot build it without you.

HELP BUILD THE MOVEMENT
https://t.co/GHAIadcCQ5
Whether the challenges before us involve socialism, threats to religious freedom, the distribution of deadly abortion drugs, or decisions made by a local government, our hope is not in politics or the government of man.

We need the Holy Spirit to bring spiritual renewal to our nation.

And when this midterm election is over, FRC's calling will remain the same: to pray and work for that renewal, from generation to generation.

Thank you for standing with us, and helping us equip believers across America to pray, vote and stand!

Donate Now
Tony Perkins
P.S. - Wilda, as a reminder, if you weren't able to join us in person this past weekend, you can catch up on all the sessions from the Pray Vote Stand Summit for free on the Stand Firm app. Be sure to share it with friends and family members, so they too can be equipped with knowledge and truth heading into the midterm elections.
